Hearing your words from the other side shows which lines sound like blame
It makes the real conversation unnecessary
quiz.explain: Playing the other person helps you feel how your words land and fix lines that sound accusing.

quiz.q: Which question belongs to the "So what?" stage of reflection?
options: What does this show about my skills and the situation?
What will I do next time?
quiz.explain: So what? is about meaning: what the event shows. What? describes; Now what? plans.

quiz.q: Aisha says "I'm just a small trader." Which change best follows Present, Past, Future?
options: Say her name, what she sells and where, her eight years' experience, and her bulk-supply goal
quiz.explain: Present, Past, Future gives who she is now, how she got there and what she is building.

quiz.q: Which is the strongest evidence of communication skill in an interview?
options: A STAR story with a real situation, actions and a result
quiz.explain: STAR gives checkable detail: situation, task, action and result.

quiz.q: Ngozi's profile total rose from 25 to 30. By about what percentage did it rise?

finalQuiz.q: Ifeoma sends "Come early" to a group about Sunday's event, and members arrive at different times. What is the best fix?
options: Send a voice note shouting at those who came late
Send the exact time and place, and ask members to reply OK
finalQuiz.explain: A specific message plus a feedback check closes the communication loop (Module 1).

finalQuiz.q: A colleague says "Fine, do it your way" and then refuses to help all week. Which style is this?
finalQuiz.explain: The disagreement is real but expressed through words that hide it and through withdrawal, which is passive-aggressive (Module 1).

finalQuiz.q: When is it right to put assertiveness scripts aside?
options: When the other person is older
When the other person has threatened or harmed you
When you are speaking in Pidgin
finalQuiz.explain: If someone has harmed or threatened you, safety comes first: seek help from trusted people or organisations (Module 1).

finalQuiz.q: Your friend says, "My shop rent went up and I don't know what to do." Which reply is active listening?
options: "So the rent rose and you're unsure of your options. What are you thinking about?"
finalQuiz.explain: It paraphrases and asks an open question instead of fixing, story-stealing or judging (Module 2).

finalQuiz.q: Which message follows all four NVC steps?
options: "You never pay on time, you are unserious."
"The ₦8,000 due on Monday hasn't come. I'm worried because I need it for stock. Can you pay by Thursday?"
finalQuiz.explain: It gives an observation, a feeling, a need and a specific request (Module 2).

finalQuiz.q: A relative keeps pushing after your clear no to a loan. What should you do?
options: Give a longer list of your expenses
Repeat your decision calmly, perhaps agreeing with any true point, without new excuses
finalQuiz.explain: Calm repetition and fogging keep your decision steady without starting an argument (Module 2).

finalQuiz.q: Which closing pattern makes a spoken request sound most sure?
options: Voice rising at the end, with a laugh
Voice dropping at the end, then a short pause
Speaking very fast to get it over with
finalQuiz.explain: A falling pitch and a pause signal a clear request (Module 3).

finalQuiz.q: In a difficult conversation, what does separating intention from impact mean?
options: Accepting she may not have meant to hurt you, while still saying you were hurt
Proving she meant to hurt you
finalQuiz.explain: Intentions and effects are different; naming both lowers defensiveness (Module 3).

finalQuiz.q: Which is SBI feedback to a helper?
options: "At Friday's party (S), you refilled the drinks before guests asked (B), and people stayed happy and relaxed (I)."
finalQuiz.explain: It names the situation, a specific behaviour and its impact (Module 3).

finalQuiz.q: Over four weeks, Bimbo had 16 chances to speak up and took 12. What is her asking rate?

options: What does this show about my habits?
What will I do differently next time?
finalQuiz.explain: Now what? turns reflection into a plan for next time (Module 4).

finalQuiz.q: Which introduction best uses Present, Past, Future?
options: "I'm Joy, a seamstress in Benin City. I've sewn school uniforms for six years. I want to supply two schools next term, so I'd love to meet school owners here."
"Hello everyone, I'm not good at speaking."
finalQuiz.explain: It covers who she is now, her experience and her goal, and ends with a link to the listeners (Module 4).

capstone.title: Assertive Communication Practice Project
capstone.brief: Plan, hold (or honestly reflect on) a real conversation from your own life using the skills in this course, show a passive or aggressive response rewritten assertively, and set a 90-day plan for your next communication challenge.
steps: Choose a real, safe situation, ideally your focus situation from Module 1.
Complete the one-page conversation plan: goal, main point, their side, neutral opening, NVC request, calm repeat and alternative, time and place.
Write your original passive or aggressive draft, explain what made it so, and write the assertive version.
Rehearse with role reversal or your phone recorder at least twice.
Hold the conversation, or if it already happened, document it honestly.
Write a What, So what, Now what reflection within 24 hours and add the journal entries from at least four weeks.
Re-score your communication profile and write a 90-day plan for one named challenge.
evidence: Dated communication profile, before and after, with totals
One-page conversation plan for a real situation
Before-and-after scripts with a note on what made the first draft passive or aggressive
What, So what, Now what reflection
Four weeks of journal entries with counts
90-day plan naming a specific challenge, weekly actions and a practice partner
